recommendation: Either rename/redefine the field to reflect 'features or PSMs without a usable sequence' and fix the doc, or count distinct features (break out of the inner loop after the first empty id, or use a per-feature flag). Implementation/doc change only; struct layout unchanged, no ABI impact.

title: compute() returns NaN means or throws on empty/partial input with no documented contract
recommendation: Guard the divisions (return 0 or NaN deliberately and documented) and the front() calls (check empty()), and document the empty-input behavior. Pure implementation change, no ABI impact.

title: Doc says 'all PeptideHits' get annotated, but only the first hit per PeptideIdentification is touched
recommendation: Fix the doc to say 'first PeptideHit of each PeptideIdentification' (source-compatible), or loop over all hits if all were intended.

title: TIC::getResults() is declared but never defined, and its type is inconsistent with compute()'s actual result
recommendation: Remove the getResults() declaration from TIC.h (the metric is stateless by design). Removing an unimplemented member is effectively source-compatible since no caller can currently link against it.

title: Default tolerance=20 is unit-blind: passing tolerance_unit=DA without tolerance gives a 20 Dalton match window
recommendation: Make the default depend on the unit (e.g. require an explicit tolerance when DA is chosen), or document that the 20 default is ppm-only and a Da tolerance must always be passed. Doc-only change is source-compatible.

title: compute() appends to the results vector with no reset; repeated calls accumulate, and getResults() has no clear()
recommendation: Document the accumulating semantics on compute()/getResults() and/or add a public clear(). Additive (add clear()) is ABI-safe; doc clarification is source-compatible.

title: Sibling exportFeatureMap() signatures disagree on whether MSExperiment is optional
recommendation: Make the two signatures consistent. Either require exp in both or default it in both. Adding a default to MQMsms is source-compatible; removing the default from MQEvidence would be a breaking source change, so prefer aligning toward the optional form.

title: fileSize returns -1 on error but the return type is unsigned, so the sentinel becomes the maximum UInt64
recommendation: Either return a signed Int64 (ABI-breaking) or, additively, document the exact sentinel value 'std::numeric_limits<UInt64>::max()' and add a named constant so callers compare correctly. At minimum, change the doc to say the sentinel is the maximum UInt64, not '-1'.

title: delta() never reports a memory decrease: the negative sign is computed then discarded
recommendation: Build the magnitude string first, then prepend the sign (use '+=' or compose 'sign + magnitude'). Internal helper fix; no API change.

title: downloadFile returns void and the actual on-disk filename is unknowable to the caller (auto-renamed to .0/.1 on collision)
recommendation: Additive, ABI-safe fix: add an overload `static std::string downloadFile(const std::string& url, const std::string& download_folder)` (or a new `downloadFileTo`) that returns the final on-disk path. Keep the existing void signature for compatibility. Document that the void overload's destination filename is non-deterministic under collisions.

title: Sibling canRun() methods (explicitly cross-referenced as analogous) have incompatible signatures and error-reporting models
recommendation: Document the divergence prominently in both headers. For convergence without breaking ABI, add overloads so each class offers both the logging form and the error_msg form. Avoid changing the existing signatures (ABI break).

title: getOutputDirOption() creates the directory on disk as a side effect of a getter
recommendation: Document the directory-creation side effect in the header (and that it may throw if creation fails), or split into a pure getOutputDirOption() plus an explicit ensureOutputDir_()/createOutputDir_() helper. Documenting is source- and ABI-compatible; splitting is additive (add new method, keep old). At minimum the surprise must be in the declared contract.

title: loadSwathFiles returns bool 'success' but most real failures throw instead of returning false
recommendation: Clarify the header @return to state explicitly that the bool reflects only the window gap/overlap check and that other errors (load failures, mixed input types) are reported via exceptions. Documentation-only; ABI-neutral.

title: Returns 0.0 for never-written pixels, indistinguishable from a true zero intensity
recommendation: Behavior is documented and ABI-stable; keep getIntensity but make the mask coupling unmissable in docs and consider an additive helper like `std::optional<double> getIntensityIfPresent(x,y)`. Additive only; no ABI break.

title: getName() returns the exception class name, getMessage() returns what(); the ctor's 'name' is the class label, not a human name
recommendation: Clarify in the header docs that getName() yields the exception class identifier and getMessage() yields the fully-formatted what() string (not the verbatim constructor argument). ABI: doc-only.

title: EPSILON is a mutable global 'constant' while its siblings (PI, E, ...) are const
recommendation: If mutability is intentional, document it as a tunable global (and note thread-safety); otherwise make it `inline const double` (or `constexpr`) to match siblings. Marking it const is potentially source-breaking for any code that assigns to it, so prefer adding a setter or documenting; abi_impact reflects the const-ification.

title: indexOf throws ElementNotFound instead of returning a not-found sentinel
recommendation: Document the throwing behavior in the header, and/or add a non-throwing companion (e.g. `tryIndexOf` returning std::optional<Size> or a sentinel) for callers doing membership-style lookups. ABI: additive overload is non-breaking.

title: Header uses Size, std::find and Exception::ElementNotFound without including the headers that define them
recommendation: Add the required includes (<algorithm>, <iterator>, OpenMS/CONCEPT/Types.h, OpenMS/CONCEPT/Exception.h) so the header is self-contained. ABI: source-compatible, additive includes only.

title: Public enum-name lookup arrays are mutable global string_view arrays, not const
recommendation: Declare these as `inline constexpr std::string_view[]` (or `static const`) so they are immutable. Const-ifying is essentially source-compatible (read accesses are unaffected) and prevents accidental global mutation.

title: Static setters mutate a process-wide singleton's last-exception state with no indication of global/thread scope
recommendation: Document the global, non-thread-safe, last-exception-wins semantics in the header; consider deprecating the public setters (they are primarily for BaseException's own bookkeeping). Also note `throw()` is a removed dynamic exception specification in C++17 and should be `noexcept`. ABI: doc + spec change are source-compatible.

title: const setLogType deletes and reallocates the logger object
recommendation: Keep the const interface for ABI stability but document explicitly that setLogType reallocates current_logger_ and is not thread-safe / must be called before sharing the object across threads. Long term, prefer a non-const setter or a smart-pointer member to make the mutation visible at the call site.

title: Nesting/recursion depth is a single static shared across ALL ProgressLogger instances and threads
recommendation: Document that recursion_depth_ is global state intended only for single-threaded nested progress and must not be relied upon across instances/threads; or make it non-static (per-instance) which would be a behavior change. ABI: making it non-static or thread-local would change layout (breaking); the doc-only fix is ABI-safe.

title: operator-> on a LogStream returns the buffer, not a self-like proxy
recommendation: Document clearly that operator-> exposes the underlying LogStreamBuf (so '->' members are buffer members, distinct from same-named LogStream methods). Renaming/removing would break call sites, so prefer a doc clarification plus, optionally, an explicitly named accessor like 'buf()'.

title: getLevel() (and rdbuf()) are non-const read-only accessors
recommendation: Add a 'std::string getLevel() const;' overload (and a const rdbuf()) as an additive, ABI-compatible change; keep the existing non-const one. Underlying level_ read is const-safe.

title: parse() builds a Param but does NOT apply any logging configuration
recommendation: This is documented, so the surprise is mitigated; consider renaming intent in docs to 'parseToParam' or adding a convenience 'parseAndConfigure(StringList)' overload that does both, to reduce the easy mistake of calling parse() alone. ABI-safe additive overload.

title: isTTY returns false for every stream except the actual std::cout/std::cerr objects
recommendation: Behavior is documented, so the main fix is to make the name self-explanatory or rename to isStdConsoleTTY()/isConsoleStream() via a deprecated alias; at minimum keep the doc note prominent. ABI-safe to add an alias.

title: Mutator id methods return Size as a 0/1 'was-changed' flag rather than the id or void
recommendation: Keep the methods (used widely) but document the return clearly; optionally add bool-returning aliases for the change-flag semantics. Do not silently repurpose the return. ABI-safe to leave as-is + doc.

title: Setter silently takes the absolute value of a negative argument
recommendation: Document that the input is normalized to its absolute value. Doc fix; ABI-safe.

title: Copy ctor and assignment are declared public but never defined, so copying link-fails instead of compile-failing
recommendation: Replace the unimplemented declarations with '= delete' so misuse is caught at compile time with a clear message. Source-compatible for correct callers; turns latent link errors into immediate compile errors.

title: Single-argument constructor is non-explicit, allowing implicit conversion from any callable to a scope-guard
recommendation: Mark the constructor explicit. Source-compatible for the intended direct-init usage 'RAIICleanup x([]{...});'; only breaks (intended) implicit conversions.

title: operator< ignores the pre-release identifier's value, breaking strict-weak-ordering semantics callers expect
recommendation: Document the intentional 'pre-release ties are order-equivalent' rule prominently on operator< and operator> (already partially noted), and warn that < equivalence does not imply ==. If full semver ordering is ever desired, add a separate comparator. Doc fix; ABI-safe.

title: getIndex returns -1 (signed) on 'not found', a sentinel easy to misuse as an index or to overflow for large vectors
recommendation: Document the -1 sentinel at the call-relevant level and keep it (changing the return type would break ABI). Optionally add a `findIndex` returning `std::optional<Size>` for new code. Doc-only is ABI-safe.

title: operator<< on a vector<string> appends (push_back) rather than stream-formats — same token means 'append' here and 'format to stream' two lines above
recommendation: Document the append-semantics clearly and scope its visibility (it currently lives in namespace OpenMS and matches any TString). Long term prefer an explicit named helper or `emplace_back` at call sites. Doc/visibility note is ABI-safe; removing the operator would be source-breaking.

title: Mutator/'-ed' copy naming pairs are inconsistent: 'remove'/'reverse'/'simplify'/'quote' have no copy variant, while trim/toUpper/substitute do
recommendation: Add the missing copying overloads (reversed, simplified, removed, etc.) as additive inline functions — purely additive, ABI-safe — so the convention is complete and predictable.

symbol: operator<(const DataValue&, const DataValue&) / operator>(const DataValue&, const DataValue&)
title: DataValue operator< / operator> order lists by size and ignore unit; inconsistent with operator==
recommendation: Document the size-based, unit-agnostic ordering in the header and warn against using DataValue as an ordered-container key. Source-compatible fix: make list ordering lexicographic, add a deterministic cross-type tiebreak, and factor unit into the order so it agrees with operator==.

title: setUnit/getUnit doc says 'String' / 'UO identifier' but the unit is an opaque int32_t the class never validates
recommendation: Fix the doc comment (remove 'String'), document that the value is a numeric CV/UO accession with -1 meaning 'no unit', and cross-reference getUnitType(). Doc-only, ABI-neutral.

title: toChar() doc implies it always returns a pointer/NULL, but it throws for non-string non-empty types
recommendation: Add an `@exception Exception::ConversionError is thrown for non-string, non-empty values` clause to the header doc (the sibling ParamValue::toChar has the same gap). Doc-only, ABI-neutral.

title: update(p_outdated) copies values FROM the argument INTO *this, opposite of the usual 'a.update(b)' direction
recommendation: Keep the API (well established) but make the direction unmissable in the brief (e.g. 'pulls still-valid values FROM the outdated arg INTO this; this is the new/current schema'). Consider an alias name like `mergeValidValuesFrom` as an additive, deprecated-aliased rename. Doc-first; ABI-neutral.

title: getSectionDescription returns an empty string for a missing section, indistinguishable from a real empty description
recommendation: Documented as-is, but flag the inconsistency: keep behavior for ABI safety and pair it with hasSection() in docs (e.g. 'use hasSection() to distinguish missing from empty'). Optionally add a throwing overload for consistency. Doc-first, ABI-neutral.

title: intersects() returns an enum on DRange but a bool on DBoundingBox; the bool 'does it intersect' query is named isIntersected() on DRange
recommendation: Document the enum return prominently and that bool conversion lumps Intersects+Inside as 'true' (Disjoint==0). Consider adding a clearly-named DRange::classifyIntersection() returning the enum and making intersects()/isIntersected() consistently bool across DRange and DBoundingBox; keep old names as deprecated aliases for ABI.

title: abs() mutates the position in place rather than returning an absolute-value copy
recommendation: Document the in-place mutation in the brief comment ('Replaces each coordinate with its absolute value, in place'). Optionally add a const 'DPosition absCopy() const' for the non-mutating expectation. Rename to makeAbs()/absInPlace() with a deprecated alias if a cleaner API is desired (ABI: additive).

title: extend(PositionType) doc says invalid min/max are 'not fixed automatically' but the code does fix them to the center
recommendation: Pure doc fix: correct the @param note to match the actual clamping-to-center behavior ('inverted ranges are collapsed to their center; min>max can never result'). No code/ABI change.

title: Non-explicit single-arg constructor allows a scalar to implicitly become a DPosition with ALL coordinates set to that scalar
recommendation: Marking explicit would be the ideal fix but is ABI/source-breaking given pervasive implicit use; instead document the fill-all-dimensions behavior prominently and add a static named factory like DPosition::filled(x) for clarity. Flag explicit as the ideal long-term fix (breaking).

title: Default-constructed interval has min=+max_double and max=-max_double, violating the class's own documented min<=max invariant
recommendation: Document explicitly that the default/empty state intentionally has inverted corners and that geometric accessors (width/height/center/diagonal) are only meaningful after at least one enlarge()/setMinMax(); soften the @invariant to exclude the empty sentinel. No ABI change.

title: operator* between two DPositions is the dot product (returns a scalar), not an element-wise vector
recommendation: Keep for ABI but make the brief comment say 'Inner (dot) product, returns a scalar' (it already says inner product, but the contrast with +/- being element-wise deserves a note). Consider a named dot() method as the discoverable form. No ABI change.

title: assign() across dimensions silently copies only the overlapping coordinates and leaves the rest untouched
recommendation: Behavior is documented; clarify in the brief that higher dimensions are left unchanged (not zeroed) and take rhs by const reference to avoid the silent copy. Minor; consider renaming to assignCommonDims(). No hard ABI break needed.

title: Non-const operator() returns a value copy, not a mutable reference; assignment through it is impossible
recommendation: Document clearly that DistanceMatrix is write-only via setValue() (because writes must maintain min_element_), and consider removing the redundant non-const operator() overload (it adds no capability). ABI: removing an overload is breaking; safest additive fix is a doc note. Do NOT change it to return a reference (would bypass min_element_ tracking).

title: Relational operators compare container sizes, not element contents, while operator== compares elements
recommendation: Rename to a clearly size-based comparator or make relational ops lexicographic to match ==. If ABI must hold, at minimum document that ordering is by size only. ABI: changing semantics is behavioral-breaking; doc + a new explicitly-named method (e.g. sizeLess) is the safe additive path.

title: Single-argument non-explicit constructor enables implicit conversion from any container to a pointer-aliasing view
recommendation: Mark the single-argument constructors `explicit`. ABI: source-compatible in most code (implicit conversions are rare and usually unintended), low risk.

title: Default-constructed MatchedIterator is NOT an end iterator (is_end_=false) despite holding singular iterators
recommendation: Either initialize the default ctor to is_end_(true) so a default iterator equals end(), or document loudly that a default-constructed iterator is singular and must be assigned before any use. ABI: changing the default flag is behavioral; the conservative additive fix is documentation, ideal fix is is_end_(true).

title: size() returns entries read so far, not the number of entries in the FASTA file
recommendation: Document is present but the name still actively misleads; consider an additive alias like entriesRead()/numCached() and deprecate reliance on size() as a total. ABI: additive method is non-breaking; renaming would break callers.

title: empty() is const on the vector specialization but non-const on the file specialization, breaking the shared interface
recommendation: Make the file specialization's empty() const (mark f_ access mutable if needed) to match the vector specialization. ABI: adding const is source-compatible for callers.

title: setTime marks a date-less DateTime as valid, so isValid() returns true for an object with no (valid) date
recommendation: Document that isValid()/isNull() track assignment, not calendar validity; or only set valid=true when the date fields already form a valid date. Prefer the doc clarification (source-compatible) given the explicit intent to mimic Qt.

title: getDate fills month,day,year (US order) while string output is yyyy-MM-dd — easily-swapped same-typed UInt out-params
recommendation: Cannot change the parameter order without breaking source. Add a strongly-named struct-returning accessor (e.g. a small {year,month,day} struct) or at least emphasize the month-day-year order in the header doc to reduce swap bugs. Additive/doc fix is source-compatible.

title: operator< ignores the 'valid' flag that operator== includes, so ordering and equality disagree
recommendation: Include fields_.valid in operator< (as the lowest-priority key) to make the ordering consistent with equality, or document the discrepancy. Adding valid to the tie is source-compatible and ABI-neutral.

title: operator+ is non-const, so it cannot be applied to a const Adduct
recommendation: Add `const` qualifier: `Adduct operator+(const Adduct& rhs) const;`. Adding const to a member is ABI-breaking on some platforms (mangled name changes); the safe additive path is to add a const overload while keeping the old one deprecated.

title: query() documented to return a negative value 'if no explanations found' but never can
recommendation: Fix the documentation to state it returns 0 when no explanations match (range is empty), removing the false negative-return contract. Pure doc change, no ABI impact.

title: Two overloads of toAdductString differ in static-ness for no reason; the 2-arg one needs an instance but uses none
recommendation: Mark the 2-arg overload `static` as well. Changing a non-static member to static is technically an ABI/mangling change; the additive-safe path is to add a new static overload (e.g. with a defaulted mol_multiplier on the static 3-arg form) and deprecate the non-static one.

title: getID() narrows a Size feature index into a signed Int, silently wrapping for large maps
recommendation: Change the return type to Size to match getFeatureIndex(), or document the narrowing. Return-type change is ABI-breaking; if stability is required, add `Size getIDSize() const` and deprecate getID(), and document the truncation on the old one.

title: getCompomer() doc says it returns an 'Id' but it returns the Compomer object
recommendation: Fix the doc-comments to 'Returns the Compomer ...' / 'Set the Compomer ...'. Pure doc change, no ABI impact.

title: Single-argument Adduct(Int) is non-explicit, enabling silent int->Adduct conversions
recommendation: Mark the constructor `explicit`. This is source-compatible for direct-initialization call sites; only code relying on implicit conversion breaks (and should). Low ABI risk (no mangling change for constructors), but could break dependent compilation, so stage with a deprecation note.

title: getError() returns a different physical unit (ppm vs Th) depending on hidden usePPM() state
recommendation: Document the unit dependence at the getError() declaration (currently the brief only says 'in either ppm or Th') and consider an explicit getErrorPPM()/getErrorTh() pair so call sites are self-documenting. Additive overloads are ABI-safe.

title: Read-only predicate hasCVReference() is not const and cannot be called on a const CVMappings
recommendation: Add a `const` overload (or change the qualifier to const). Adding the const qualifier is source-compatible for existing callers; the safest ABI-preserving route is to add a new `bool hasCVReference(const std::string&) const;` overload.

title: getStatus() doc numbering contradicts the actual SolverStatus enum values
recommendation: Fix the doc-comment to reference the actual enumerators (UNDEFINED/OPTIMAL/FEASIBLE/NO_FEASIBLE_SOL) instead of stale magic numbers, and steer callers to compare against the enum rather than ints. Doc-only change; no ABI impact.

title: Name-lookup 'get' methods mutate the GLPK problem object (build a search index)
recommendation: Document that the lookup builds/refreshes a name index as a side effect (and is therefore non-const and not cheap if called in a loop). If desired, build the index lazily once. Doc-only; no ABI impact.

title: Pure read-only solution/bound/objective getters are not const
recommendation: Mark the genuinely read-only accessors const (or add const overloads). Adding const is source-compatible; because these are virtual-free non-overloaded members, prefer adding const directly with care for the GLPK index-building exceptions noted separately.

title: readProblem documents its input filename as @param[out] and ignores 'format' for most backends
recommendation: Change the doc tag to `@param[in] filename` and reword the description (it reads, not stores). Document that 'format' is only honored by the GLPK backend (or remove/deprecate the parameter where ignored). Doc-only; no ABI impact.

title: fromNativeID takes a signed int but transition/native IDs are UInt32 everywhere else in the class
recommendation: Add a `UInt fromNativeID(UInt32 transition_id) const` overload to match getTransition()/getID() typing, and deprecate the int version. Additive overload is source-compatible.

title: applyFunctionOnPeptideHits/IDs default to ALSO mutating unassigned identifications
recommendation: Document the default prominently in the doc-comment (currently '/// applies a function on all PeptideHits or only assigned ones' does not state the default) so callers know unassigned IDs are included unless they pass false. Doc-only; no ABI/source impact. Changing the default would be a behavior break, so keep it and document.

title: Ion-mobility unit accessors return the literal placeholder "?" instead of a real unit
recommendation: Document explicitly in the header that the IM unit is intentionally unknown and that these accessors return "?" as a sentinel; ideally add a bool-returning hasKnownUnit()/isUnitKnown() helper (additive, source-compatible) so callers can branch instead of string-matching "?". Do not silently emit "?" into user-facing labels.

symbol: Peak2D::shortDimensionName / fullDimensionName / shortDimensionUnit / fullDimensionUnit (and MobilityPeak2D equivalents)
title: Dimension accessors taking a UInt index do no bounds checking and silently read out of bounds for dim>=2
recommendation: Add an assert/range check that throws Exception::IndexOverflow for dim>=DIMENSION (or OPENMS_PRECONDITION), matching OpenMS index-access conventions. This is source-compatible; the only behavior change is converting UB into a defined throw for already-invalid input.

title: getMobility() is documented as "access to m/z" (copy-paste from Peak1D), contradicting the function name and behavior
recommendation: Fix the doc comment to "Non-mutable access to the mobility". Documentation-only change, no ABI impact.

title: RTLess compares left.getRT() against right.getPos() instead of right.getRT()
recommendation: Change right.getPos() to right.getRT() for consistency with the comparator name and the sibling comparators. Behavior-preserving today; source-compatible.

title: getBins() returns a raw owning pointer that can be nullptr on default-constructed objects
recommendation: Document that getBins() may return nullptr for default-constructed objects, or return a reference and guarantee allocation, or expose helper accessors (nonZeros(), bin count) so callers never touch the raw pointer. ABI: doc-only is non-breaking; signature change would break.

title: getMZ() on a chromatogram returns product-precursor metadata, not anything derived from the peak data
recommendation: Consider an additive, clearer alias such as getProductMZ() (deprecate-and-alias getMZ) to make the source of the value explicit; at minimum keep the doc note. ABI: additive alias.

title: Two emplace_back overloads with inconsistent return types (one returns a reference, the variadic returns void)
recommendation: Make both overloads return `MobilityPeak1D&` (and use std::forward in the variadic form) to match std::vector semantics; drop the by-value single-arg overload in favor of the variadic. ABI: changing return type of an inline is source-compatible for typical call sites.

title: erase() returns a ConstIterator, unlike std::vector::erase which returns a mutable iterator
recommendation: Return Iterator (the mutable iterator that data_.erase already yields) to match std::vector and the sibling classes. ABI: return-type change on an inline is source-compatible for assignment-style call sites.

title: Docs say peaks are sorted 'Lexicographically' but the sort uses a single scalar key
recommendation: Drop 'Lexicographically' from the docs (or specify the tie-break behavior, which is stable order). Doc-only. ABI: none.

title: findNearest overloads disagree on return type and failure mode (Size+throw vs Int+(-1) sentinel)
recommendation: Keep the signatures (ABI) but emphasize in docs the differing contracts; longer term consider an std::optional<Size>-returning additive overload for a uniform not-found signal. ABI: doc now; additive overload later.

title: const getMetaData() hands out a non-const shared_ptr<PeakMap> to internal meta state
recommendation: Add a getMetaData() const overload returning std::shared_ptr<const PeakMap> and, if mutation is genuinely needed, a separate non-const getMetaData(). Changing the return type is source-breaking, so introduce the const-returning variant additively and deprecate the mutable one.

title: getSpectrum() silently returns a peak-less spectrum when filtered, indistinguishable from a genuinely empty scan
recommendation: Document the empty-means-filtered contract directly on getSpectrum() (currently only in the class header), and consider an explicit wasFiltered(id) or an optional out-param so callers can distinguish filtered-out from genuinely empty. Additive only; do not change the return type.

title: aggregate() returns an empty vector for both 'no ranges' and 'no spectra at this MS level', erasing per-range output structure
recommendation: On the 'no matching spectra' path, return a vector of size mz_rt_ranges.size() of empty sub-vectors (preserving positional indexing), or document the size-0 contract prominently. Behavioral change, so gate behind doc + possibly a new overload.

title: calculateTIC returns a top-level const value, defeating move semantics
recommendation: Drop the top-level const on the return type (return MSChromatogram). This is source-compatible for nearly all callers but changes the function signature/mangling; provide as an additive cleanup in a minor release.

title: const getter returns a mutable reference into the object and lazily recomputes/caches internal state
recommendation: Additive/source-compatible: add a `const ConvexHull2D& getConvexHull() const;` overload (or change the return type to const-ref) so callers cannot mutate the cache, and document that the first call lazily recomputes the overall hull. If the mutable return is genuinely needed, provide it via a distinctly named non-const method (e.g. getMutableConvexHull()). Keep the lazy-cache behavior but state it in the docstring.

title: const getAnnotationState() copies and sorts peptide hits internally; ID-format selection is non-obvious
recommendation: Document that the method sorts copies of the peptide IDs (so it is O(n log n), not a trivial query) and that new-format matches take precedence over legacy peptide IDs when both are present. No ABI change needed.

title: operator+= silently resets the LHS's ranges, document identifier and unique id
recommendation: The header doc mentions DocumentIdentifier/UniqueIdInterface reset but not the range reset; document that ranges are invalidated (call updateRanges() afterward). Behavior is load-bearing, so prefer documentation over a behavior change to preserve ABI.

title: size() returns the number of chromatograms, not transitions or features, even though the group holds several parallel collections
recommendation: Document size() as 'number of fragment-ion chromatograms' and/or add getTransitions().size()-style named accessors; no rename needed. ABI: doc-only, none.

title: clear() defaults to also wiping ALL metadata (column headers, protein/peptide IDs, ranges, unique id, experiment type), unlike std::vector::clear
recommendation: Keep the overload but consider documenting prominently that the default destroys all run/column/ID metadata; callers wanting std::vector semantics must pass false. A safer default (false) would be a behavior break, so prefer doc emphasis. ABI: none (doc).

title: setRatios takes a non-const lvalue reference, blocking temporaries/const args despite only copying
recommendation: Add a const-ref overload (and/or an rvalue overload) so it matches normal setter ergonomics; keep the existing one for ABI. ABI: additive overload is none/additive.

title: Plain getters getMin()/getMax() throw on an empty/default-constructed range
recommendation: Keep throwing for safety but make it discoverable: document the throw on every derived getMinRT/getMinMZ/etc. (currently only the base mentions it), and offer a non-throwing companion such as getNonEmptyRange() (already exists) or a tryGetMin(). Doc/additive change; ABI-safe.

title: RangeManager::extend(RangeManager) throws when dimensions do not overlap, unlike every other extend overload
recommendation: Document the throw prominently on extend/assign/clampTo/pushInto (the brief says only '@throw ... if no dimensions overlapped'). Consider that the *Unsafe naming is inverted vs. typical 'unsafe = no checks'; a future additive rename to extendOrNothing()/tryExtend() with a deprecated alias would reduce surprise. Doc-only fix is ABI-safe.

title: The 'Unsafe' suffix denotes 'does not throw', the opposite of its usual C++ meaning
recommendation: Clarify in the docs that 'Unsafe' here means 'does not throw on no-overlap; caller must check the bool return'. Ideal additive fix: introduce tryExtend()/extendIfOverlap() aliases and deprecate the *Unsafe names. Doc-only is ABI-safe.

title: Area stores a non-owning DimMapper pointer; copies share it and outliving the mapper dangles
recommendation: Prominently document the borrowed-lifetime contract on the constructor (caller must keep the DimMapper alive for the lifetime of every Area and its clones). The '(non owning pointer)' comment is on the ctor but the danger to copies/clones should be explicit. Doc-only; ABI-safe.

title: subtractMinimumIntensity mutates intensities in place and leaves data arrays inconsistent
recommendation: Promote the 'data arrays are not updated' note from a code comment into the declaration's doxygen so callers see it in the API docs. No ABI change needed.

title: MS level type is inconsistently signed (uint8_t in ctor, int8_t in setter and member)
recommendation: Unify on uint8_t for the setter parameter and the ms_level_ member to match the constructor and the domain (MS levels are non-negative). Internal:: class, so the signedness change is low-risk; verify no caller relies on negative sentinel.

title: Pressure/flux accessors are UInt but the backing members are signed Int (negative values round-trip as huge UInt)
recommendation: Make member types match the public unsigned API (store UInt) or make the API signed to match the members; either way pick one. ABI-safe path: keep signatures, change member declarations to `UInt`, which is a non-ABI-affecting internal change and removes the silent sign reinterpretation.

title: Doc-comments for organism/number/state accessors are copy-paste wrong ('returns the sample name')
recommendation: Fix the doc-comments to describe organism/number. Doc-only change, fully ABI-safe.

title: getCurrentProcessingStep is a non-const getter, so it cannot be called on a const IdentificationData
recommendation: Add a `const` overload `ProcessingStepRef getCurrentProcessingStep() const;` (additive). The ProcessingStepRef is an IteratorWrapper over a set::iterator that can be obtained from a const member without exposing mutability of the set's elements (set elements are const anyway), so this is safe and ABI-additive.

title: isNativeID recognizes the 'frame=' prefix that getRegExFromNativeID handles, but the class doc table omits 'frame=' from both
recommendation: Add 'frame=' to the documented recognized-prefix list (and the class CV table) so the doc matches behavior. Doc-only fix; no ABI impact.

title: 'estimate' return-flag semantics are documented inconsistently (true vs '1' vs false) and on failure the object is left in a partially-built state
recommendation: Fix the doc typo so all three methods read 'true = ok, false = negative hydrogens requested', and document that on false the formula_ is left without H (or restore prior state). abi_impact: doc-only.

title: contains() doc says elements of ef must be 'LESS abundant' than this, but the predicate is actually '>=' (less-or-EQUAL) and the direction wording is reversed-sounding
recommendation: Reword doc to: 'returns true if, for every element in ef, this has at least as many atoms (>=, equality allowed); i.e. this contains ef as a sub-formula'. abi_impact: doc-only.

title: Element exposes full mutators, but every Element a caller can obtain is owned by the singleton ElementDB and handed out as const Element* (immutable by design)
recommendation: Document on Element that instances vended by ElementDB are immutable/shared and must not be mutated; consider clarifying that setters are only for constructing custom Elements not registered in the DB. abi_impact: doc-only.

title: operator< orders by name only, but operator== compares name+synonyms+regex+description
recommendation: Document that operator< is a name-only ordering and is not consistent with operator== (or make operator< tie-break on the same fields == uses). Behavior change to operator< could affect sorted containers, so prefer documenting the contract; field-aligning the comparison is source-compatible but a subtle behavior change.

title: peptideCount is non-const although it only reads state, while the heavier digest() is const
recommendation: Add `const` to peptideCount. This is source-compatible for callers but changes the mangled name (ABI). Prefer adding a const overload or marking const in the next ABI-breaking window; documenting is the conservative interim fix.

title: RNA-enzyme string getters return by value while base-class string getters return const ref
recommendation: For consistency and to avoid copies, change to `const std::string&` returns (source-compatible for most callers, but changes ABI/mangling). At minimum document the by-value choice. Conservative: leave as-is and note the inconsistency.

title: Sibling lookup-by-key methods throw different exception types for the not-found case
recommendation: Standardize both on Exception::ElementNotFound (the regex case is genuinely 'element not found'). This is source-compatible at the call site if callers catch the common base; document if a change is deferred.

title: getMax()/getMin() document "returns the isotope" but return only a coordinate (m/z double)
recommendation: Reword the doxygen to "returns the m/z of the isotope with the largest/smallest m/z" (the value, not the isotope). If a peak is genuinely wanted, add getMaxPeak()/getMinPeak() returning Peak1D for symmetry with getMostAbundant(). Doc fix is ABI-safe; adding overloads is additive.

title: getRoundMasses() doc contradicts setRoundMasses()/class semantics about what true vs false means
recommendation: Fix the getRoundMasses() doxygen to match the setter: true => integer-rounded masses, false => accurate masses. Pure doc fix, no ABI impact.

title: trimLeft/trimRight trim by container position (not by mass), and silently assume the distribution is mass-sorted
recommendation: Document that these operate on the current (assumed mass-sorted) ordering and call sortByMass() first if unsure; or have them sort internally. Doc fix is ABI-safe.

title: estimateFrom*/estimateForFragment* are non-const despite not mutating the generator, breaking const-correctness symmetry with run()
recommendation: Mark the read-only estimate* methods const to match run() and the const fragment overloads. Adding const can be source-compatible but is technically an ABI/overload change for a non-virtual member; prefer doing it in a coordinated minor-version bump, or at minimum document the inconsistency.

title: const predicate compatible() writes diagnostic text to std::cerr
recommendation: Remove the leftover debug `cerr` statement (it looks like forgotten debugging output). This is a pure source/ABI-compatible change of an inline-less .cpp body; no signature change. If logging is intended, route it through OPENMS_LOG_DEBUG instead of unconditional std::cerr.

title: operator*= mutates its const-reference argument via const_cast
recommendation: ABI-safe: operate on a local copy of the RHS instead of const_casting the caller's object, so the const contract is honoured. No signature change.

title: operator== compares against a string and parses it, but there is no operator== against another MassDecomposition
recommendation: ABI-safe additive: add `bool operator==(const MassDecomposition&) const` (and !=) so type-to-type equality is available and matches operator<. Keep the string overload but note it parses on each call.

title: Index-based accessors do no bounds checking and read out of range on a bad index (UB), while the name-based siblings throw a clean exception
recommendation: ABI-safe: document that the index overloads require 0 <= index < size() and are unchecked (UB otherwise), making the asymmetry with the throwing name overloads explicit. Optionally add a checked accessor. No signature change needed.

title: annotateMatches Doxygen in/out param directions are swapped (the const input is marked [out], the mutated output marked [in])
recommendation: Swap the Doxygen directions: '@param[in,out] spec' (mutated) and '@param[in] ph' (read-only). Pure doc fix, no ABI impact.

title: Doxygen marks the read-only input oligo as [out]
recommendation: Change '@param[out] oligo' to '@param[in] oligo'. Pure doc fix, no ABI impact.

title: Doc promises a throw on a 'STRICT' policy that does not exist in the ConversionPolicy enum
recommendation: Fix the doc to reference FAIL_ON_LOSS (the throwing policy) and the actual exception type thrown. abi_impact none.

title: getMonoWeight(Peptidoform) silently ignores the peptidoform's own per-chain charge field
recommendation: Either add a getMZ(const Peptidoform&) overload that uses pf.charge (symmetry with PeptidoformIon), or document that pf.charge is ignored by the mass/m-z helpers and must be passed explicitly. abi_impact source-compatible if adding an overload.

title: computeHydrophobicMoment hardcodes the Eisenberg scale while sibling profile methods take a configurable scale parameter
recommendation: Document in the header that the hydrophobic moment is computed on the Eisenberg consensus scale (per Eisenberg 1984), and optionally add a scale parameter overload. abi_impact none for doc; source-compatible if adding an overload.

title: MzPAFParseError stores context_before_/context_after_ but exposes no getters, unlike the sibling ProForma::ParseError
recommendation: Add getContextBefore()/getContextAfter() accessors to MzPAFParseError for parity. abi_impact source-compatible (additive).

title: Non-virtual destructor on a class explicitly documented as a base class
recommendation: Make the destructor virtual (additive, but ABI-breaking because it changes the vtable layout) OR document explicitly that derived objects must never be deleted through a CVTermListInterface* and consider protecting the destructor. At minimum the misleading 'use to inherit from' doc and non-virtual dtor should be reconciled.

title: replaceCVTerms map overload takes a non-const lvalue reference unlike every sibling
recommendation: Deprecate the non-const overload and rely on the const-ref map overload (they are redundant). Removing it is ABI-breaking; making it const is also a signature change. Safest additive step: mark the non-const one [[deprecated]] and route callers to the const overload.

title: hasCVTerm documented as 'checks whether the term has a value' but checks accession presence
recommendation: Fix the doc comment to 'checks whether a CV term with the given accession is present' in both headers. Doc-only, fully ABI compatible.

title: getCVTerms documented as 'returns the accession string of the term'
recommendation: Correct the doc comment in both headers to describe the returned map. Doc-only, ABI compatible.

title: Plain value struct CVTerm::Unit has a virtual destructor, giving it a surprising vtable
recommendation: Make the destructor non-virtual (ideally = default and non-virtual) since Unit is not a base class. Changing virtual->non-virtual is ABI-breaking (vtable removal), so guard behind a deliberate ABI-break window; otherwise document that the virtual is vestigial.

title: Container exposes add/insert/resize but no element removal (no clear/erase/pop_back)
recommendation: Additively export the missing symmetric members ('using ContainerType::clear; using ContainerType::erase; using ContainerType::pop_back;' and likely front/at/reserve) to complete the container surface. Purely additive, source- and ABI-compatible.

title: getSample is a read-only lookup but is declared non-const
recommendation: Add const qualifier. Since this changes the mangled name, ideally add a const overload (or change to const if no callers rely on the non-const binding) and deprecate the non-const form.

title: getNumberOfFractions documented as 'highest fraction index' but returns count of distinct fraction ids
recommendation: Update the doc to 'number of distinct fraction identifiers'. Documentation-only; no ABI impact.

title: getPrimaryMSRunPath returns an empty string for unknown identifier or out-of-range merge index
recommendation: Document the empty-string-means-not-found contract in the header, or add a tryGetPrimaryMSRunPath(...) bool overload (consistent with the existing tryGetIdentifier pattern) so callers can detect failure. Additive; no ABI break.

title: setStart() documented as setting the position of the *last* AA (copy-paste error from setEnd)
recommendation: Fix the doc comment to say "position of the FIRST AA of the peptide" (start), purely a comment change. abi_impact none.

title: setSequence()/setAccession() silently trim() the input, so the stored value differs from what was passed
recommendation: Document the trimming in the header comments for setSequence/setAccession (and the constructor). abi_impact none (doc only).

title: setModifications takes a non-const lvalue reference, so const sets and temporaries cannot be passed
recommendation: Add an overload taking `const std::set<...>&` (additive, source-compatible); ideally deprecate the non-const-ref signature. abi_impact source-compatible.

title: empty() ignores RT, MZ, spectrum_reference and hits' annotations — a spectrum-anchored ID with metadata reports empty()==true
recommendation: Document precisely what empty() considers, or add the RT/MZ/spectrum_reference checks behind a clearly named method (e.g. hasContent()). abi_impact none for doc; source-compatible if a new method is added.

title: hasMZ() is documented as "shortcut for isnan(getRT())" (copy-paste from hasRT)
recommendation: Fix the comment to "shortcut for !isnan(getMZ())" (and note both comments say isnan but the methods return the negation). abi_impact none.

title: get*Ref() accessors throw when the variant holds a different molecule type
recommendation: Document the throwing precondition (must match getMoleculeType()) in the header, and consider adding non-throwing `tryGetIdentified*Ref()` variants returning std::optional. Additive, ABI-safe.

title: Read-only predicate isInResidueSet() is not const
recommendation: Add `const` to the declaration and definition. Adding const is source-compatible for callers but changes the mangled symbol, so technically an ABI break for that one symbol; provide it as the canonical fix and rebuild dependents.

title: Doc comments say 'returns a pointer' but both return a const reference
recommendation: Fix the doc comments to 'returns a (const) reference to the residue ... throws Exception::IndexOverflow if out of range'. Doc-only, ABI-safe.

title: Doc says getLossNames() returns 'an empty string' but it returns a vector of strings
recommendation: Fix the doc to 'returns the neutral loss names (empty vector if none)'. Doc-only, ABI-safe.

title: getMonoWeight(type, charge) returns a proton-added neutral-plus-charge mass, not an m/z, despite a sibling getMZ existing
recommendation: Header already says 'in the given ionic form'; strengthen the doc to state explicitly that a non-zero charge adds charge*proton mass (charged-species mass, not m/z, not neutral). Doc-only, ABI-safe.

title: get(index) is a non-const getter and cannot be called on a const NASequence
recommendation: Add `const` to the existing method (or add a const overload to preserve ABI): `const Ribonucleotide* get(size_t index) const`. The implementation already only reads, so marking it const is source-compatible for existing non-const callers.

title: length handling is inconsistent: getSubsequence clamps an over-long length, getPrefix/getSuffix throw
recommendation: Pick one convention (preferably clamp, consistent with getSubsequence) and apply it across all three, or document the divergence prominently. Aligning getPrefix/getSuffix to clamp is source-compatible for valid inputs.

title: getSubsequence (a const accessor) prints to std::cout
recommendation: Remove the stray `cout` line. Pure cleanup, no API/ABI change.

title: Doc comments for getAvgMass/setAvgMass are swapped (getter documented as 'Set', setter as 'Get')
recommendation: Swap the two doc comments so each describes its own method. Documentation-only fix, no ABI impact.

title: Doc claims count is "read from the unimod.xml file" but it counts all providers plus runtime-interned mods
recommendation: Reword doc to "Returns the total number of modifications currently in the database (all providers plus any runtime-added)." ABI-safe doc fix.

title: Parameter named keep_original in header, keep_unmodified in impl; doc claims original is the "first entry" but output is appended to an existing vector
recommendation: Make the header and impl parameter name agree, and change the doc to "...as the first appended entry". ABI-safe (parameter names are not part of ABI; doc-only).

title: Override silently changes the 'search-eligible' criterion and drops thread-safety vs the base class with the same name
recommendation: Document the differing criterion in the header explicitly, and add the `#pragma omp critical(OpenMS_ModificationsDB)` around the mods_ iteration to match the base class's thread-safety contract. Lock addition and doc are ABI-safe.

title: encodeNPRaw with np_compression==NONE returns leaving `result` empty/unmodified, indistinguishable from a real failure
recommendation: Document explicitly that NONE is a no-op that leaves result untouched, distinct from failure, so callers don't treat empty output as an error (or vice versa). ABI-safe doc-only fix; no signature change needed.

title: decodeLinear returns size_t but documents returning -1 on bad size; -1 becomes a gigantic unsigned count
recommendation: Vendored code, so prefer not to change the signature for upstream-sync reasons; at minimum correct the doc to say the sentinel is `(size_t)-1` == SIZE_MAX (not a negative number) and that callers MUST guard dataSize >= 8 before use. Doc-only, no ABI impact.

title: Base64.h force-exports a symbol literally named `compress` from the DLL on MSVC, colliding with zlib's global compress()
recommendation: Document why this export exists (it works around zlib `compress` not being re-exported for pyOpenMS/plugins) directly at the pragma, and if possible scope it to the single TU that needs it rather than a public header so every includer doesn't inherit the export. Build-system change; no source ABI of OpenMS classes affected.

title: decodeSingleString omits the zlib_compression default that every other decode* method provides, breaking the call-convention pattern of the class
recommendation: Add `= false` to decodeSingleString's zlib_compression parameter to match the rest of the class. Adding a default argument is source-compatible and not an ABI change.

title: GzipIfstream docs reference bzip2 and the wrong file extension (*.gzip)
recommendation: Fix the doc to say gzip and '.gz'. Pure documentation change, no ABI impact.

title: store() is non-const although it only reads the internal buffer
recommendation: Mark store() const (and CsvFile::store). This is source-compatible for callers but changes the mangled signature, so it is technically an ABI break on the symbol; if strict ABI must be preserved, add a const overload or defer to the next ABI-breaking release.

title: getTypeByFileName documents @exception FileNotFound but never touches the filesystem
recommendation: Fix the doc: remove the '@exception FileNotFound' line from getTypeByFileName (it is a copy-paste from getTypeByContent). This is a doc-only, source/ABI-compatible change. Do NOT add an existence check — callers rely on the pure-string behavior (e.g. for output filenames that do not yet exist).

title: storeSpectrum takes a non-const MSSpectrum& even though it only writes (does not modify) the spectrum
recommendation: Change the parameter to 'const MSSpectrum& spec' to match the other store* methods and allow storing const/temporary spectra. This is source-compatible for almost all callers (a const-ref is more permissive) but technically an ABI/signature change; do it at the next ABI break or add a const-ref overload now.

title: loadIdentifications neither clears nor uniformly appends; the OMSSAXML path indexes additional_proteins[0] after a single push_back, corrupting prior contents on a non-empty vector
recommendation: Change the OMSSAXML branch to load into additional_proteins.back() (matching PROTXML), so 'additional' semantics hold for all formats. This is an internal bug fix, source/ABI-compatible. Also document in the header whether loadIdentifications appends or replaces (currently unstated).

title: store() takes its source map by non-const reference (cannot store a const map)
recommendation: Add a `store(const std::string&, const PeakMap&)` overload (additive, source-compatible) so const maps can be stored consistently with the other File classes; fix the `@param[out]` doc tags to `@param[in]`.

title: store() silently overwrites the user-configured WriteIndex option on the object
recommendation: Apply WriteIndex(true) to a local copy of the options passed to the consumer/MzMLFile rather than mutating the persistent member options_ (source- and ABI-compatible internal change).

title: Copy constructor silently drops the stream position and does not copy chrom_index/filename_cached state
recommendation: Add `filename_cached_(rhs.filename_cached_)` to the initializer list and verify the freshly-opened stream's state (additive/internal; source- and ABI-compatible).

title: transform() signature drifts between MzMLFile and MzXMLFile (extra skip_first_pass bool)
recommendation: Document the divergence; if parity is desired, add the skip_first_pass overload to MzXMLFile (additive, source-compatible). The two adjacent bools are inherently swap-prone — consider an enum/flags type in any new overload.

title: isValid() throws NotImplemented on a default-constructed instance instead of returning a bool
recommendation: Document is sufficient for ABI stability, but the throw-from-a-bool-predicate based on construction state is the surprise; consider asserting/documenting that derived classes must bind a schema. ABI-safe (doc-only).

title: getCentroidInfo() (a 'get' method) opens/parses a file and temporarily mutates the object's options
recommendation: Doc-only / naming: the I/O cost is implied by the filename arg, but the transient options_ mutation is non-obvious — note it is not thread-safe w.r.t. concurrent option reads. ABI-safe.

title: store(ConsensusMap) documented "NOT IMPLEMENTED" but is fully implemented
recommendation: Source-compatible doc-only fix: remove the "NOT IMPLEMENTED" line from the Doxygen block and document the actual output format. No ABI change. (The inverse risk — callers who coded around a believed no-op — is why the stale doc is dangerous.)

title: store() takes a parameter named 'spectrum' although load() reads/writes a FeatureMap; it also unconditionally throws
recommendation: Source-compatible: keep the throw but rename/retype the unused parameter to `const FeatureMap&` (or document it) so the not-implemented stub matches the format's data model; or drop the cerr print since the thrown exception already signals it. No external ABI surface (templated, always throws).

title: Doxygen marks the output PeakMap exp as @param[in] and lists params in an order that does not match the signature
recommendation: Doc-only fix: reorder to match signature and mark `@param[out] exp`. No ABI impact.

title: store() second parameter named/typed 'SpectrumType spectrum' while load() uses 'FeatureMapType feature_map'
recommendation: Rename store()'s template parameter and argument to FeatureMapType/feature_map to match load(). Header-only template, so this is source-compatible and ABI-neutral.

title: setPosition() returns a bool whose meaning is undocumented and not obviously a success flag
recommendation: Document the @return contract (true = seek succeeded / stream good) in the header. Doc-only, ABI-neutral.

title: loadSize() neither loads data nor returns a byte size; it parses to count features
recommendation: Add a Doxygen comment clarifying it returns the feature count (not bytes) and that it parses the whole file; consider renaming to countFeatures()/getNumberOfFeatures() in a future ABI-breaking cleanup with the old name kept as a [[deprecated]] alias. Doc addition is ABI-neutral; rename is breaking.

title: PEFFEntry getter getSequence()/getModifiedSequence() can throw on malformed sequence content
recommendation: Document the throwing behavior (@exception) on getSequence()/getModifiedSequence(), or provide a non-throwing variant returning an optional/empty AASequence. Doc addition is ABI-neutral.

title: ProtXMLFile::store is a fully declared public method whose only behavior is to throw NotImplemented
recommendation: Keep throwing (the feature is unimplemented), but fix the doc: replace the @exception UnableToCreateFile line with '@exception Exception::NotImplemented is always thrown (writing protXML is not supported)'. Ideally mark the method [[deprecated("protXML writing not implemented")]] or remove it until implemented; removal is breaking, so the doc fix is the ABI-safe path.

title: PepXMLFile::store takes protein_ids/peptide_ids by NON-const reference but never modifies them; inconsistent with sibling store() methods
recommendation: Change the two parameters to const references to match IdXMLFile/MzIdentMLFile/ProtXMLFile. This is source-compatible for callers passing non-const lvalues but is technically an ABI/signature change (mangled name changes). If strict ABI must be preserved, add a new const overload and forward; deprecate the non-const one.

title: PTMXMLFile::store is a const method but takes ptm_informations by NON-const reference, falsely implying it may mutate the map
recommendation: Change the parameter to 'const std::map<...>&'. Note PTMXMLHandler's ctor also takes a non-const ref (shared load/store ctor), so this requires either a const ctor overload or a const_cast at the boundary. Source-compatible for existing callers but changes the mangled signature (ABI). If ABI-frozen, add a const-map overload.

title: PepXMLFile::store doc says 'Stores idXML as PepXML file' but the method writes pepXML; @exception text mentions wrong condition
recommendation: Doc-only, ABI-safe: reword the brief to 'Stores the given identifications as a pepXML file'. No signature change.

title: matchModification_ doc tags 'mass' as @param[in,out] and the description param is documented [out] in the wrong slot
recommendation: Doc-only, ABI-safe: change to '@param[in] mass' and '@param[out] modification_description'. This is a protected helper, so impact is limited to maintainers, but the inverted in/out tags are actively misleading.

title: "PrecursorErrorType" getter/setter actually control the precursor mass TYPE (mono/average), not an error/tolerance type
recommendation: Rename to `setPrecursorMassType`/`getPrecursorMassType` (matching the member `precursor_mass_type_` and the doc) for clarity. ABI-break to rename; ABI-safe path is to add the correctly-named methods as inline forwarders and deprecate the misnamed pair. At minimum, fix the header parameter name to `mass_type`.

title: Write-only bool options with no matching getter, unlike sibling option pairs in the same class
recommendation: Add the missing const getters `getSemiCleavage()` and `getAllowIsotopeError()`. This is purely additive and ABI-safe.

title: Output identification containers documented @param[in]; load() silently clears them
recommendation: Mark these `@param[out]`, document that load() clears them first, and fix the Doxygen name mismatch (`id_data` -> `peptide_identifications`). Documentation-only, ABI-safe.

title: "getModifications" returns via an out-parameter while every sibling Infile getter returns by const reference
recommendation: Add an overload (or new method) returning `const std::map<std::string,std::string>&` to match the sibling convention; keep the out-param version for ABI stability. Purely additive, ABI-safe.

title: Serialization method is named write() here but store() in every sibling *Infile class
recommendation: Provide a `store(const std::string&)` alias for cross-class consistency (ABI-safe additive), and/or document the two bool flags clearly. Renaming write()->store() would be an ABI break, so prefer the alias.

title: Doc says 'loads only results which exceeds a given P-value threshold' but it keeps records BELOW/at the threshold
recommendation: Fix the Doxygen brief and the @param text to say records with p-value <= threshold are retained (lower p-value = more significant). Behavior is correct for p-values; only the documentation contradicts it. Documentation-only change: abi_impact none.

title: load() appends to id_data instead of clearing it, unlike sibling Percolator load()
recommendation: Make the clear-vs-append contract consistent across the *Outfile/*File loaders. Either clear id_data at the start of load() (matching PercolatorOutfile) or document the append semantics in the header. Adding a clear() is source-compatible behavior change; abi none.

title: Doxygen tags the input filename as [out] and the actual output containers' direction is also mislabeled
recommendation: Correct the @param[in]/@param[out] tags: result_filename, p_value_threshold, database_filename are [in]; peptide_identifications, protein_identification are [out]. Documentation-only; abi none.

title: load() mutates the caller's SpectrumMetaDataLookup by registering reference-format regexes
recommendation: Document in the header that load() seeds default reference formats into lookup when it has none, so callers reusing the lookup across formats understand the persistent mutation. Documentation-only; abi none.

title: extra_scores is documented as @param[out] but is read-only input (const&), misleading the direction contract
recommendation: Change the Doxygen tag for extra_scores to @param[in]. Documentation-only; the const& already protects the caller. abi none.

title: getExperiment is a heavyweight I/O + file-type-detection routine, not a cheap accessor as 'get' implies, and resets its out-params
recommendation: Consider renaming to loadExperiment()/readExperiment() to signal I/O, or at minimum document that it performs content-based type detection and a full file load and resets the out-parameters. A rename is breaking; doc + a deprecated alias is the additive path. Documentation-only fix abi none.

title: load() overwrites/replaces the passed MzTab rather than the more cautious clear-then-fill being explicit; pre-populated sections are clobbered or stale
recommendation: Document that load() requires a fresh MzTab, or have load() reset all sections (assign empty NUC/OLI/OSM) before filling. Behavior fix in the .cpp; no ABI change.

title: MzTabMFile provides store() but no load() - a write-only *File adapter
recommendation: Document the write-only nature in the class brief, or add a load() to match MzTabFile. Purely additive; no ABI impact.

title: setMSFile silently ignores index 0 instead of signaling the invalid 1-based value
recommendation: Document the 1-based contract in the header and, on index==0, throw Exception::InvalidValue or at least OPENMS_LOG_WARN instead of silently no-op'ing. Behavior fix; no ABI change.

title: addPepEvidenceToRows operates on the single *this row and overwrites fields (name says add-to-Rows)
recommendation: Rename to something like `setPepEvidenceFields` / `fillFromPepEvidence` (keep the old name as a deprecated inline forwarder for ABI). Doc-only fix is the minimal step; rename is source-compatible if a forwarder is kept.

title: loadSqMass omits the tmp/readoptions parameters every other SwathFile loader has
recommendation: Document explicitly in the header that loadSqMass ignores readoptions/tmp by design (it streams from the SQLite DB), so the asymmetry is intentional and visible. A future-additive overload accepting (file, tmp, exp_meta, readoptions) for signature parity would be source- and ABI-compatible.

title: transform exposes two dead bool parameters that have no effect
recommendation: Keep them for ABI but consider [[maybe_unused]] and a clearer name, or deprecate the overload and add a 2-arg transform. Removing the params would be ABI-breaking; the documented @note already mitigates, so this is low severity.

title: load()'s filename is documented as @param[out]
recommendation: Swap the direction tags: filename -> @param[in], data object -> @param[out]. Doc-only, ABI-safe.

title: getRunID throws on zero runs too, but doc only mentions 'more than one run'
recommendation: Update the doc/throw message to cover the 'no run' case (e.g. 'requires exactly one run'), and initialize id to avoid relying on the throw. Doc + impl change, ABI-safe.

symbol: SqliteConnector::tableExists / columnExists / countTableRows / executeStatement / prepareStatement / getDB
title: Read-only query helpers are non-const, so they can't be called on a const SqliteConnector
recommendation: Add const overloads (or make tableExists/columnExists/countTableRows const) for the read-only query helpers. Adding const member functions is source-compatible but changes the mangled symbols / vtable-independent ABI of those inline methods; since they are inline header methods the practical ABI risk is low.

title: @param[out] index on a by-value Size index parameter
recommendation: Fix the direction tags: swath_result -> @param[in,out], index -> @param[in]. Doc-only, ABI-safe.

title: Class doc advertises 'Zip / unzip of Parquet directory bundles' as a capability, but no zip/unzip methods exist in the public API
recommendation: Either remove the zip/unzip bullet from the brief or expose the documented archive helpers as public static methods. Doc-only change is ABI-neutral.

title: load() is static while store() is a non-static member, and the flatHierarchy member only affects store
recommendation: Make load() a non-static member for symmetry with store() and the other *File classes, or document that load is static and unaffected by flatHierarchy. Converting static→non-static changes the mangled name (ABI break for the static symbol) — if ABI must hold, keep static but clearly document the asymmetry; the clean fix is a non-static load.

title: Doxygen tags store()'s param as @param[in,out] but it is const Param& (read-only)
recommendation: Change the Doxygen direction to `@param[in] param`. Doc-only fix, ABI-neutral.

title: Doxygen marks store()/writeXMLToStream() param (and the output stream) as @param[out] when they are read-only inputs
recommendation: Tag param as `@param[in]` in both store() and writeXMLToStream(); keep os_ptr as `[out]`. Same wrong-direction tags appear in ParamCTDFile and ParamCWLFile store/write methods (`@param[out] param`/`@param[out] tool_info` against const&) and should be fixed identically. Doc-only, ABI-neutral.

title: flatHierarchy member doc is garbled and applies only to writing, not loading
recommendation: Fix the wording to match ParamCWLFile ('listed without nesting (flattened, names include the hierarchy)') and state explicitly it only affects store()/writeToStream(), not load(). Doc-only, ABI-neutral.

title: run() returns void and swallows every failure into an out-of-band error flag
recommendation: ABI-safe minimum: document in the header that run() never throws and that callers MUST check hasError()/getErrorMessage() afterward. Better (source-compatible): add a `bool runChecked()` returning success, or have run() throw on hard failures. Keep the existing void run() for ABI but redirect it.

title: run() silently clears previously fetched responses/identifier via updateMembers_()
recommendation: Document that run() resets all prior results up front. If unintended, move the result-clearing out of updateMembers_() (which is meant for param sync) into run()'s success path only, or clear lazily.

title: transform() (streaming-consumer API) actually loads the entire file into memory first
recommendation: The @note already documents this honestly (good). Keep the note prominent until true streaming exists; consider naming/marking it so callers don't assume constant-memory. No ABI change needed.

title: exists*QualityParameter() is named like a bool predicate but returns void via an out-parameter
recommendation: Additive fix: add a bool-returning overload/companion (e.g. hasRunQualityParameter(...)) and keep the void out-param version for ID retrieval, or rename the retrieval method to getRunQualityParameterIDs(...). Pure rename is source-breaking; prefer adding the bool helper. No ABI removal needed.

title: Third 'filename' argument has a default value defined only in the .cpp, invisible/unusable from the header
recommendation: Move the default to the header declaration (and remove it from the definition). Source-compatible and makes the two-arg call usable by all TUs; no ABI change.

title: Pure read-only counter getters are non-const
recommendation: Add `const` to both declarations and definitions. This is technically an ABI change to the virtual signature (mangled name changes), so for strict ABI stability add const-qualified overloads or schedule for the next ABI-breaking release; mark honestly as source-compatible for most callers, ABI-breaking for the vtable.

title: consume methods document @param[out] s but operate on a copy, never writing back to the caller's object
recommendation: Change the doc annotation from `@param[out] s` to `@param[in] s` (it is effectively read-only). Pure doc fix; ABI-neutral. Note the cross-class inconsistency (mutates vs copies) for callers writing generic IMSDataConsumer code.

title: buffer_size is a signed int stored/compared as unsigned size_t (flush_after_), so a negative buffer flushes on every element
recommendation: Use an unsigned type (Size/size_t) for the parameter or validate `buffer_size > 0`, and align the .cpp parameter name with the header (buffer_size). Changing the parameter type is ABI-breaking; a guard/clamp inside the body is ABI-neutral and prevents the wrap-around surprise.

title: Input-only `decoy` flag is documented as @param[out]
recommendation: Change tag to @param[in]. Documentation-only; no ABI impact. (The fact that it is a bare bool that also flips use_exact_mass off internally — cpp:266 `if (decoy) use_exact_mass = false;` — is a separate hidden side effect worth a note in the doc.)

title: Input-only `decoy_generation` flag documented as @param[out]
recommendation: Retag as @param[in]. Documentation-only; no ABI impact.

title: consumeChromatogram clears the caller's chromatogram, but the doc only says it appends
recommendation: Update the header comments to state that both the spectrum and chromatogram arguments are cleared after consumption (matching the IMSDataConsumer [in,out] contract). Documentation-only; no ABI impact.

title: consumeChromatogram throws if a chromatogram's native ID has no matching transition/precursor metadata
recommendation: Document in the header that consumeChromatogram throws Exception::InvalidValue when the chromatogram's native ID cannot be matched to the transition experiment. Documentation-only; no ABI impact.

title: MzDataHandler constructor doc-comments label read vs write backwards
recommendation: Swap the two doc comments so the non-const overload reads 'read-only handler' and the const overload reads 'write-only handler', matching MzMLHandler.h:100-104 and MzXMLHandler.h:46-50. Comment-only change, no ABI impact.

title: setSkipXMLChecks parameter named 'only' contradicts its meaning
recommendation: Rename the header parameter from `only` to `skip` to match the implementation and the member semantics. Parameter-name-only change; no ABI impact.

title: reset() documented to 'release internal memory' is an empty no-op in the base class
recommendation: Either remove the dead method or implement it to clear `open_tags_`, `sm_`, `cv_terms_`, etc.; at minimum finish the doc comment and state it is a no-op unless overridden. Removing would be breaking; documenting/implementing is non-breaking.

title: getOptions() returns a non-const reference to internal options with no const counterpart
recommendation: Add an additive `const PeakFileOptions& getOptions() const;` overload to MzMLHandler (and MzXMLHandler/MzDataHandler which expose no getter at all) to match the FeatureXML/ConsensusXML convention. Purely additive; no ABI break.

title: Doxygen @param directions are wrong: the output vector is tagged [in] and the input 'indices' is tagged [out]
recommendation: Doc-only fix: change to @param[out] exp and @param[in] indices for both methods. No ABI or source impact.

title: Write methods tag a const-ref INPUT experiment as @param[out]
recommendation: Doc-only fix: change @param[out] to @param[in] for both. No ABI/source impact.

title: Class is documented 'Read-only accessor' but all three read methods are non-const
recommendation: Add const to the three read methods (each opens its own connection on demand per the constructor doc, so there is no logical mutation). const-qualification changes the mangled symbol, so this is technically ABI-breaking on these symbols; safe to do for an Internal class but should be flagged. Source-compatible for callers.

title: FidHandler publicly inherits std::ifstream, exposing the raw stream API (seekg/read/close) alongside its index-tracking methods
recommendation: Prefer composition (hold an ifstream member) or protected/private inheritance so the raw cursor cannot be moved out from under index_. This changes the type's public base and is ABI/source-breaking, so for an Internal class flag it as the ideal fix; short term, document that callers must not use the inherited ifstream positioning API.

title: Doc comments for the attribute-name setters are copy-pasted from setAccessionAttribute and describe the wrong attribute
recommendation: Fix the doc comments to describe the name and value attributes respectively. Comment-only change; no ABI/source impact.

title: Set/Get doc labels are swapped on all three numpress configuration accessor pairs
recommendation: Swap the Set/Get words so each label matches its method, and add a note to setNumpressConfigurationMassTime that it warns on std::cerr for lossy SLOF/PIC configs. Comment-only change; no ABI/source impact.

title: Boolean setters declare their parameter as 'only', unrelated to what the flag controls
recommendation: Rename the header parameters to match the implementation (fill/always_append/skip). Parameter-name changes are source- and binary-compatible.

title: preprocess_ overwrites every hit score and flips score type/orientation in the input
recommendation: Document on the override that it rewrites scores/score-type/orientation in place (the one-line '/// Assign peptide scores based on search ranks' undersells this). Since apply() already replaces ids wholesale this is benign for the standard path, but the misleadingly-named override plus the intentionally-incorrect isHigherScoreBetter flag is a trap for anyone calling preprocess_ directly. Additive doc fix; no ABI change.

title: bool consistency-check return value is meaningless: it is always true or it throws
recommendation: Either make it void (and rely on the throw for failure) or remove the throw so the bool is meaningful. Since this is a private method, changing to void is internal-only (no public ABI impact). Update the '@return all same?' doc accordingly.

title: Sibling method warning references a non-existent method name 'mergeAllProteinRuns'
recommendation: Fix the warning text to name the real method mergeAllIDRuns. Pure string/doc fix; no ABI impact.

title: keep_matching documented as @param[in,out] but is a by-value bool (cannot be an output)
recommendation: Change the Doxygen tag from @param[in,out] to @param[in] for keep_matching in both overloads. Documentation-only; ABI-neutral.

title: Read-only getters returning const-ref are not declared const; unusable on a const RipFileContent
recommendation: Add trailing const to both getters. This is source-compatible for callers but is technically an ABI-affecting signature change (mangled name changes); for strict ABI stability add new const overloads instead of editing in place.

title: run() clears pre-existing protein groups / indistinguishable-protein lists without saying so
recommendation: Document the clearing in the run() Doxygen (the @param[in,out] note only mentions scores/counts), and/or only clear when grouping is actually going to be recomputed. Doc-only fix is ABI-safe.

title: Read-only 'get' accessors are non-const, blocking const-correct use
recommendation: Add const qualifiers (getProteinIDs() const, getNrConnectedComponents() const). Because these are virtual-free non-inline members, adding const changes the mangled name = ABI break; schedule for next ABI-breaking release or provide const overloads alongside.

title: Constructor validates model probabilities only via assert(), so out-of-range params are silently accepted in release builds
recommendation: Replace asserts with Exception::InvalidValue (or at minimum OPENMS_PRECONDITION) so invalid probabilities are rejected consistently. Constructor-body change is ABI-safe. Note: class is in namespace Internal (semi-public via templated header).

title: Declared parameter names (id, pep_id) are swapped relative to the implementation names (nId, pepId)
recommendation: Align names: rename the header params to nId/pepId (or vice versa) and document that the first Label is the parent-count/sum variable and the second the peptide variable. Doc/name-only, ABI-safe.

title: Doc says '30%' but the gating threshold for a positive match is 80% of affixes plus 30% of proteins, and per-string success uses different cutoffs
recommendation: Fix the header doc comment to state the real criteria (>=80% of affix occurrences and >=30% of proteins, with a 30% gross floor). Doc-only, abi-neutral.

title: Pure-lookup query methods are non-const, blocking use on const instances
recommendation: Add const to isScoreTypeHigherBetter and getScoreNames. Adding const to a member function is source-compatible (it changes the mangled name, so technically an ABI change for those two symbols).

title: Input tolerance parameter is doxygen-tagged [out]
recommendation: Change the tag to `@param[in]`. Pure documentation fix, ABI-neutral.

title: peptide_ids and feature_set are documented @param[in] but are mutated outputs
recommendation: Re-tag peptide_ids and feature_set as `@param[in,out]` (and feature_set arguably `@param[out]`). Pure documentation fix; ABI-neutral.

title: concat...() mutates the 'source' new_peptide_ids (writes CONCAT meta values) and appends to all_peptide_ids, both tagged [in]
recommendation: Re-tag all_peptide_ids and new_peptide_ids as `@param[in,out]` and note in the brief that new_peptide_ids hits gain CONCAT meta values. Doc-only; ABI-neutral.

title: 'check' verb hides that extra_features is mutated (entries erased)
